shloka_text: स मुहूर्तादुपश्रुत्य देवर्षिरमितप्रभः । स्वमाश्रमं शिष्यवृतः क्षुधार्तः सन्न्यवर्तत ।। 7.81.1 ।।
transliteration: sa muhūrtādupaśrutya devarṣiramitaprabhaḥ | svamāśramaṃ śiṣyavṛtaḥ kṣudhārtaḥ sannyavartata || 7.81.1 ||
translation: सः he, मुहूर्तात् after a short while, उपश्रुत्य having heard, देवर्षिः the divine sage, अमितप्रभः of immeasurable splendor, स्वम् his own, आश्रमम् hermitage, शिष्यवृतः surrounded by disciples, क्षुधार्तः afflicted by hunger, सन्न्यवर्तत he returned.
explanation: After a short while, the divine sage of immeasurable splendor, surrounded by his disciples and afflicted by hunger, returned to his hermitage, having heard (something amiss).
comments: The returning Bhrigu, learning of the outrage, curses Danda to perish within seven nights with all his realm under a rain of dust -- having removed the hermits to safety and bidden Araja dwell unharmed by the lake, the curse falls and the whole kingdom is reduced to ashes, thereafter called Dandakaranya, or Janasthana -- and Agastya sends Rama to his evening prayers as the sun sets.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यदरजां दीनां रजसा समभिप्लुताम् । ज्योत्स्नामिव ग्रहग्रस्तां प्रत्यूषे न विराजतीम् ।। 7.81.2 ।।
transliteration: so 'paśyadarajāṃ dīnāṃ rajasā samabhiplutām | jyotsnāmiva grahagrastāṃ pratyūṣe na virājatīm || 7.81.2 ||
translation: सः he, अपश्यत् he saw, अरजाम् Arajā, दीनाम् distressed, रजसा with impurity, समभिप्लुताम् covered, ज्योत्स्नाम् moonlight, इव like, ग्रहग्रस्ताम् eclipsed, प्रत्यूषे at dawn, न not, विराजतीम् shining.
explanation: He saw Arajā, distressed and covered with impurity, like moonlight eclipsed by a planet and not shining brightly at dawn.

shloka_text: तस्य रोषः समभवत्क्षुधार्तस्य विशेषतः । निर्दहन्निव लोकांस्त्रीञ्छिष्यांश्चैतदुवाच ह ।। 7.81.3 ।।
transliteration: tasya roṣaḥ samabhavatkṣudhārtasya viśeṣataḥ | nirdahanniva lokāṃstrīñchiṣyāṃścaitaduvāca ha || 7.81.3 ||
translation: तस्य his, रोषः anger, समभवत् arose, क्षुधार्तस्य of the hungry one, विशेषतः especially, निर्दहन्निव as if burning, लोकान् worlds, त्रीन् three, शिष्यान् to the disciples, च and, एतत् this, उवाच said, ह indeed.
explanation: His anger, especially due to hunger, arose as if burning the three worlds, and he spoke this to his disciples.

shloka_text: पश्यध्वं विपरीतस्य दण्डस्याविजितात्मनः । विपत्तिं घोरसङ्काशां क्रुद्धामग्निशिखामिव ।। 7.81.4 ।।
transliteration: paśyadhvaṃ viparītasya daṇḍasyāvijitātmanaḥ | vipattiṃ ghorasaṅkāśāṃ kruddhāmagniśikhāmiva || 7.81.4 ||
translation: पश्यध्वं behold, विपरीतस्य of the perverse, दण्डस्य of Daṇḍa, अविजितात्मनः of the uncontrolled one, विपत्तिं the calamity, घोरसङ्काशां terrible-looking, क्रुद्धां enraged, अग्निशिखाम् a flame of fire, इव like.
explanation: Behold the terrible calamity, like an enraged flame of fire, that will befall the perverse and uncontrolled King Daṇḍa.

shloka_text: क्षयो ऽस्य दुर्मतेः प्राप्तः सानुगस्य दुरात्मनः । यः प्रदीप्तां हुताशस्य शिखां वै स्प्रष्टुमिच्छति ।। 7.81.5 ।।
transliteration: kṣayo 'sya durmateḥ prāptaḥ sānugasya durātmanaḥ | yaḥ pradīptāṃ hutāśasya śikhāṃ vai spraṣṭumicchati || 7.81.5 ||
translation: क्षयः destruction, अस्य of this, दुर्मतेः evil-minded one, प्राप्तः is imminent, सानुगस्य with his followers, दुरात्मनः of the wicked one, यः who, प्रदीप्तां blazing, हुताशस्य of fire, शिखां a flame, वै indeed, स्प्रष्टुम् to touch, इच्छति desires.
explanation: The destruction of this evil-minded and wicked one, along with his followers, is imminent, for he desires to touch a blazing flame of fire.

shloka_text: यस्मात्स कृतवान्पापमीदृशं घोरसंहितम् । तस्मात्प्राप्स्यति दुर्मेधाः फलं पापस्य कर्मणः ।। 7.81.6 ।।
transliteration: yasmātsa kṛtavānpāpamīdṛśaṃ ghorasaṃhitam | tasmātprāpsyati durmedhāḥ phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ || 7.81.6 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, सः he, कृतवान् has committed, पापम् a sin, ईदृशं such, घोरसंहितम् a terrible one, तस्मात् therefore, प्राप्स्यति will obtain, दुर्मेधाः the foolish one, फलं the fruit, पापस्य of the evil, कर्मणः deed.
explanation: Because he has committed such a terrible sin, that foolish one will therefore receive the consequence of his evil deed.

shloka_text: सप्तरात्रेण राजासौ सभृत्यबलवाहनः । पापकर्मसमाचारो वधं प्राप्स्यति दुर्मतिः ।। 7.81.7 ।।
transliteration: saptarātreṇa rājāsau sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ | pāpakarmasamācāro vadhaṃ prāpsyati durmatiḥ || 7.81.7 ||
translation: सप्तरात्रेण within seven nights, राजा king, असौ that, सभृत्यबलवाहनः with his servants, army, and vehicles, पापकर्मसमाचारः whose conduct is sinful, वधं death, प्राप्स्यति will meet, दुर्मतिः the evil-minded one.
explanation: Within seven nights, that evil-minded king, whose conduct is sinful, will meet his death along with his servants, army, and vehicles.

shloka_text: समन्ताद्योजनशतं विषयं चास्य दुर्मतेः । धक्ष्यते पांसुवर्षेण महता पाकशासनः ।। 7.81.8 ।।
transliteration: samantādyojanaśataṃ viṣayaṃ cāsya durmateḥ | dhakṣyate pāṃsuvarṣeṇa mahatā pākaśāsanaḥ || 7.81.8 ||
translation: समन्तात् all around, योजनशतम् a hundred yojanas, विषयम् the region, च and, अस्य of this, दुर्मतेः evil-minded one, धक्ष्यते will burn, पांसुवर्षेण by a dust shower, महता great, पाकशासनः Paka-shasana (Indra).
explanation: Shukra declares that Indra will destroy the evil-minded Daṇḍa's region, extending a hundred yojanas in all directions, with a mighty shower of dust.

shloka_text: सर्वसत्वानि यानीह स्थावराणि चराणि च । महता पांसुवर्षेण विलयं सर्वतो ऽगमन् ।। 7.81.9 ।।
transliteration: sarvasatvāni yānīha sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca | mahatā pāṃsuvarṣeṇa vilayaṃ sarvato 'gaman || 7.81.9 ||
translation: सर्वसत्वानि all beings, यानि which, इह here, स्थावराणि immobile, चराणि mobile, च and, महता by a great, पांसुवर्षेण dust shower, विलयम् destruction, सर्वतः completely, अगमन् reached.
explanation: All beings, both mobile and immobile, present in that region, completely met their destruction due to the great shower of dust.

shloka_text: दण्डस्य विषयो यावत्तावत्सर्वसमुच्छ्रयम् । पांसुवर्षमिवालक्ष्यं सप्तरात्रं भविष्यति ।। 7.81.10 ।।
transliteration: daṇḍasya viṣayo yāvattāvatsarvasamucchrayam | pāṃsuvarṣamivālakṣyaṃ saptarātraṃ bhaviṣyati || 7.81.10 ||
translation: दण्डस्य of Daṇḍa, विषयः the region, यावत् as far as, तावत् so far, सर्वसमुच्छ्रयम् all elevated things, पांसुवर्षम् a dust shower, इव like, अलक्ष्यम् imperceptible, सप्तरात्रम् for seven nights, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: For seven nights, the entire region of Daṇḍa, including all elevated structures, will become imperceptible, as if covered by a continuous shower of dust.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा क्रोधताम्राक्षस्तदाश्रमनिवासिनम् । जनं जनपदान्तेषु स्थीयतामिति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.81.11 ।।
transliteration: ityuktvā krodhatāmrākṣastadāśramanivāsinam | janaṃ janapadānteṣu sthīyatāmiti cābravīt || 7.81.11 ||
translation: इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, क्रोधताम्राक्षः with eyes red with anger, तदाश्रमनिवासिनम् to the residents of that hermitage, जनम् the people, जनपदान्तेषु at the borders of the country, स्थीयताम् let it be stayed, इति thus, च and, अब्रवीत् he said.
explanation: Having spoken thus, Shukra, whose eyes were red with anger, instructed the people residing in that hermitage to stay at the borders of the country.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तूशनसो वाक्यं सो ऽ ऽश्रमावसथो जनः । निष्क्रान्तो विषयात्तस्मात्स्थानं चक्रे ऽथ बाह्यतः ।। 7.81.12 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tūśanaso vākyaṃ so ' 'śramāvasatho janaḥ | niṣkrānto viṣayāttasmātsthānaṃ cakre 'tha bāhyataḥ || 7.81.12 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, उशनसः of Ushanas, वाक्यम् the word, सः that, आश्रमावसथः hermitage-dwelling, जनः people, निष्क्रान्तः departed, विषयात् from the region, तस्मात् from that, स्थानम् place, चक्रे made, अथ then, बाह्यतः outside.
explanation: Having heard the words of Ushanas (Shukra), the people dwelling in that hermitage then departed from that region and established their abode outside.

shloka_text: स तथोक्त्वा मुनिजनमरजामिदमब्रवीत् । इहैव वस दुर्मेधे आश्रमे सुसमाहिता ।। 7.81.13 ।।
transliteration: sa tathoktvā munijanamarajāmidamabravīt | ihaiva vasa durmedhe āśrame susamāhitā || 7.81.13 ||
translation: सः He, तथा thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, मुनिजनम् to the sages, अरजाम् to Araja, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् said, इह एव here itself, वस dwell, दुर्मेधे O foolish one, आश्रमे in the hermitage, सुसमाहिता well-composed.
explanation: Having thus spoken to the sages, he then said to Araja, "O foolish one, dwell here in this hermitage, well-composed."

shloka_text: इदं योजनपर्यन्तं सरः सुरुचिरप्रभम् । अरजे विज्वरा भुङ्क्ष्व कालश्चात्र प्रतीक्ष्यताम् ।। 7.81.14 ।।
transliteration: idaṃ yojanaparyantaṃ saraḥ suruciraprabham | araje vijvarā bhuṅkṣva kālaścātra pratīkṣyatām || 7.81.14 ||
translation: इदम् This, योजनपर्यन्तम् extending for a yojana, सरः lake, सुरुचिरप्रभम् of very beautiful splendor, अरजे O Araja, विज्वरा free from distress, भुङ्क्ष्व enjoy, कालः च and time, अत्र here, प्रतीक्ष्यताम् let it be awaited.
explanation: O Araja, enjoy this lake, which extends for a yojana and possesses a very beautiful splendor, free from distress, and let time pass here.

shloka_text: त्वत्समीपे च ये सत्त्वा वासमेष्यन्ति तां निशाम् । अवध्याः पांसुवर्षेण ते भविष्यन्ति नित्यदा ।। 7.81.15 ।।
transliteration: tvatsamīpe ca ye sattvā vāsameṣyanti tāṃ niśām | avadhyāḥ pāṃsuvarṣeṇa te bhaviṣyanti nityadā || 7.81.15 ||
translation: त्वत्समीपे near you, च and, ये those, सत्त्वाः beings, वासम् dwelling, एष्यन्ति will come, ताम् that, निशाम् night, अवध्याः invulnerable, पांसुवर्षेण by the shower of dust, ते they, भविष्यन्ति will be, नित्यदा always.
explanation: And those beings who come to dwell near you for that night will always be invulnerable to the shower of dust.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा नियोगं ब्रह्मर्षेः सा ऽरजा भार्गवी तदा । तथेति पितरं प्राह भार्गवं भृशदुःखिता । इत्युक्त्वा भार्गवो वासमन्यत्र समकारयत् ।। 7.81.16 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā niyogaṃ brahmarṣeḥ sā 'rajā bhārgavī tadā | tatheti pitaraṃ prāha bhārgavaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitā | ityuktvā bhārgavo vāsamanyatra samakārayat || 7.81.16 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा Having heard, नियोगम् the command, ब्रह्मर्षेः of the Brahmarshi, सा she, अरजा Araja, भार्गवी the daughter of Bhargava, तदा then, तथा इति "So be it", पितरम् to her father, प्राह said, भार्गवम् to Bhargava, भृशदुःखिता greatly distressed; इति उक्त्वा having said this, भार्गवः Bhargava, वासम् dwelling, अन्यत्र elsewhere, समकारयत् caused to be made.
explanation: Greatly distressed, Araja, the daughter of Bhargava, then said "So be it" to her father, the Brahmarshi, after hearing his command; having said this, Bhargava then arranged for his dwelling elsewhere.

shloka_text: तच्च राज्यं नरेन्द्रस्य सभृत्यबलवाहनम् । सप्ताहाद्भस्मसाद्भूतं यथोक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना ।। 7.81.17 ।।
transliteration: tacca rājyaṃ narendrasya sabhṛtyabalavāhanam | saptāhādbhasmasādbhūtaṃ yathoktaṃ brahmavādinā || 7.81.17 ||
translation: तत् च And that, राज्यम् kingdom, नरेन्द्रस्य of the king, सभृत्यबलवाहनम् with servants, army, and vehicles, सप्ताहात् within seven days, भस्मसाद्भूतम् turned into ashes, यथा उक्तम् as spoken, ब्रह्मवादिना by the speaker of Brahman.
explanation: And that kingdom of the king, along with its servants, army, and vehicles, was reduced to ashes within seven days, just as the sage had foretold.

shloka_text: तस्यासौ दण्डविषयो विन्ध्यशैवलयोर्नृप । शप्तो ब्रह्मर्षिणा तेन वैधर्म्ये सहिते कृते ।। 7.81.18 ।।
transliteration: tasyāsau daṇḍaviṣayo vindhyaśaivalayornṛpa | śapto brahmarṣiṇā tena vaidharmye sahite kṛte || 7.81.18 ||
translation: तस्य his, असौ this, दण्डविषयः region of Daṇḍa, विन्ध्यशैवलयोः of Vindhya and Śaivala, नृप O king, शप्तः cursed, ब्रह्मर्षिणा by the Brahmarṣi, तेन by him, वैधर्म्ये unrighteousness, सहिते accompanied, कृते having been done.
explanation: O king, this region of Daṇḍa, situated between the Vindhya and Śaivala mountains, was cursed by that Brahmarṣi when unrighteousness was committed there.

shloka_text: ततः प्रभृति काकुत्स्थ दण्डकारण्यमुच्यते । तपस्विनः स्थिता ह्यत्र जनस्थानमतो ऽभवत् ।। 7.81.19 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prabhṛti kākutstha daṇḍakāraṇyamucyate | tapasvinaḥ sthitā hyatra janasthānamato 'bhavat || 7.81.19 ||
translation: ततः from then, प्रभृति onwards, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, दण्डकारण्यम् Daṇḍaka forest, उच्यते is called, तपस्विनः ascetics, स्थिताः resided, हि indeed, अत्र here, जनस्थानम् Janasthāna, अतः therefore, अभवत् became.
explanation: O Kakutstha, from that time onwards, this region is called Daṇḍakāraṇya, and because ascetics resided here, it also became known as Janasthāna.

shloka_text: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्मां पृच्छसि राघव । सन्ध्यामुपासितुं वीर समयो ह्यतिवर्तते ।। 7.81.20 ।।
transliteration: etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yanmāṃ pṛcchasi rāghava | sandhyāmupāsituṃ vīra samayo hyativartate || 7.81.20 ||
translation: एतत् this, ते to you, सर्वम् all, आख्यातम् has been told, यत् which, माम् me, पृच्छसि you ask, राघव O Raghava, सन्ध्याम् twilight prayer, उपासितुम् to perform, वीर O hero, समयः time, हि indeed, अतिवर्तते is passing.
explanation: O Raghava, I have told you all that you asked me, but O hero, the time for performing the twilight prayer is indeed passing.

shloka_text: एते महर्षयः सर्वे पूर्णकुम्भाः समन्ततः । कृतोदका नरव्याघ्र आदित्यं पर्युपासते ।। 7.81.21 ।।
transliteration: ete maharṣayaḥ sarve pūrṇakumbhāḥ samantataḥ | kṛtodakā naravyāghra ādityaṃ paryupāsate || 7.81.21 ||
translation: एते these, महर्षयः great sages, सर्वे all, पूर्णकुम्भाः with full water pots, समन्ततः all around, कृतोदकाः having performed water rituals, नरव्याघ्र O tiger among men, आदित्यम् the sun god, पर्युपासते are worshipping.
explanation: O tiger among men, all these great sages, with their water pots full and having performed their water rituals, are worshipping the sun god all around.

shloka_text: स तैर्ब्राह्मणमभ्यस्तं सहितैर्ब्रह्मवित्तमैः । रविरस्तं गतो राम गच्छोदकमुपस्पृश ।। 7.81.22 ।।
transliteration: sa tairbrāhmaṇamabhyastaṃ sahitairbrahmavittamaiḥ | ravirastaṃ gato rāma gacchodakamupaspṛśa || 7.81.22 ||
translation: सः he, तैः by them, ब्राह्मणम् the Brahman, अभ्यस्तम् practiced, सहितैः together with, ब्रह्मवित्तमैः by the best knowers of Brahman, रविः the sun, अस्तम् setting, गतः has gone, राम O Rama, गच्छ go, उदकम् water, उपस्पृश touch.
explanation: O Rama, the sun has set, having been worshipped by those best knowers of Brahman who recite the Vedas; therefore, go and perform your ablutions. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकाशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 81 ।। Thus ends the eighty-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
